issues.title: Unsupported full-scheme second-order convergence claim

failure_location.quote:
This substitution 
enables the development of a tailored quadrature scheme, which restores the desired 
order of convergence of the entire numerical scheme.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: eq: intro - upper bound of the L=0000E9vy measure
eq: integral disc - Taylor approximation of the integrand
tab: test - Parameters sets used in the numerical experiment

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Clearly, the favourable result is found that the numerical scheme achieves second-order convergence for each set of parameters.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the tailored quadrature restores second-order convergence of the entire numerical scheme throughout the stated regime. The old paper actually supplies the quadrature construction and empirical second-order results for four selected parameter sets, but no full-scheme convergence argument. The revised analysis establishes only an integral-discretization bound of O(h_z^{2-A_ell}) for 0<A_ell<2 and O(h_z^{2-epsilon}) for A_ell=0. Thus both the guaranteed rate and the object covered by the guarantee are materially narrower than the old prose claims.
issues.overall_effect: The main-contribution discussion overstates the rigorously supported asymptotic accuracy. The algorithm and reported numerical observations remain, but general second-order convergence of the full scheme is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the general second-order convergence claim for the entire numerical scheme and replace it with the supported statements: second-order convergence was observed for the four reported parameter sets, while the proved result concerns only the truncated integral discretization and gives O(h_z^(2-A_ell)) for 0<A_ell<2 and O(h_z^(2-epsilon)) for A_ell=0. Retaining the original claim would instead require a full consistency, stability, and convergence analysis of all spatial, temporal, interpolation, truncation, and iterative components.
issues.why_classification: No local repair establishes the advertised second-order guarantee for the full scheme. The available replacement changes both the covered object and, generally, the rate, so no recognizably comparable rigorous version of the recorded claim survives. Recovering the original guarantee would require global convergence architecture, while withdrawing it entails major mathematical loss.

issues.title: Missing density-variation hypothesis for the weighted midpoint rule

failure_location.quote:
This substitution 
enables the development of a tailored quadrature scheme, which restores the desired 
order of convergence of the entire numerical scheme.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we assume that $\ell$ is absolutely continuous

diagnostic_evidence.tag: eq: intro - upper bound of the L=0000E9vy measure

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims restored convergence under the density assumptions stated in version 1. Those assumptions control the magnitude of ell near zero but not its derivatives or cellwise oscillation. In R_z^{II}, the weights integrate hat ell=ell||z||^2 while sampling hat f=f/||z||^2 at cell centers; cancellation of the linear term in hat f requires control of the first variation of hat ell. No such control follows from the old assumptions, so the advertised uniform rate is unsupported for rough densities admitted there. Version 2 adds a bound on the first derivatives of ell and assumes sufficient smoothness in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The quadrature remains executable, but its advertised convergence behavior is not justified over the full density class allowed by version 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a density-variation hypothesis sufficient for the weighted midpoint estimate, such as differentiability of ell with |partial_j ell(z)| bounded by C'_ell(h)||z||^(-3-A_ell) near the origin, restrict the convergence assertion to that smooth-density class, and supply the contained weighted-midpoint error estimate using this bound.
issues.why_classification: The old magnitude bound does not control weighted first moments within cells, and rough densities admitted by the advertised class can invalidate the claimed rate. Adding derivative control is therefore substantive rather than a typo or an exceptional-case qualification. It nevertheless leaves the quadrature construction and its convergence behavior intact on a recognizably comparable smooth-density class and requires only a contained local analysis, not global reconstruction.

issues.title: One-dimensional finite-variance formula in a two-dimensional model
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims to state the finite-variance hypothesis for the two-dimensional Lévy process, but its displayed formula is a one-dimensional integral involving scalar z^2. The old model actually uses a Lévy measure on R_*^2, for which the corresponding scalar second-moment condition is the integral of ||z||^2 over R_*^2. The old formula therefore does not express the claimed hypothesis for the stated process.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-variance assumption is locally malformed, although the surrounding two-dimensional setup makes the intended condition evident and no later formal result depends on the literal scalar formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the scalar formula by the uniquely forced two-dimensional condition integral over R_*^2 of ||z||^2 ell(dz) < infinity.
issues.why_classification: The surrounding source consistently defines a two-dimensional process and a Levy measure on R_*^2, which uniquely determines the corrected domain and norm-squared integrand. No proof or later construction uses the erroneous one-dimensional expression, so an adept reader can correct it without repairing any inference.

issues.title: Singular covariance admitted by inverse-based NTS formulas

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a given positive semi-definite symmetric matrix $\rho$

issues.failure_explanation: Under the active appendix setup, rho may be any positive-semidefinite symmetric matrix. The NTS table then claims a Lévy-density formula through Phi, while Phi and its induced norm require rho^{-1} and divide by the square root of det(rho). Singular positive-semidefinite matrices therefore make these displayed quantities undefined. Restricting rho to positive definite matrices removes precisely those inadmissible inputs.
issues.overall_effect: For singular rho, the NTS Lévy-density and density formulas and the later proposition on its bounds are not well-defined, although the underlying degenerate time-changed Brownian construction can itself still exist. Positive-definite cases and the numerical experiments are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict rho to be positive definite wherever the inverse- and determinant-based NTS Levy-density, density, and bound formulas are asserted, and propagate that premise to the dependent proposition. If singular time-changed Brownian models are retained, state separately that these full-dimensional density formulas do not cover them.
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local nondegeneracy correction: positive definiteness makes rho inverse, det(rho), and the induced norm well-defined while leaving every displayed formula and bound unchanged in the regular case. The dependent proposition and numerical experiments are repaired by the same premise, with no new construction, rate change, or material loss of the intended nondegenerate NTS regime.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: $\sqrt{\rho}$  is obtained by the Cholesky decomposition of a given positive definite symmetric matrix $\rho$, i.e. $\rho=\sqrt{\rho}\cdot\sqrt{\rho}^{\top}$.
